notes.text:
This update for gcc7 fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-95619: libstdc++ integer overflow in `new` operator (bsc#1282500).
- CVE-2026-102010: UAF due to improper pointer update when an application calls the `erase_if` function on a binary heap
  priority queue in `libstdc++` (bsc#1283123).
notes.title: Description of the patch

notes.text: A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

notes.text: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.
